players.product: regulated transmission & distribution utilities (ComEd, PECO, BGE, PHI) interconnecting data-center load in PJM

quarterly_data.signal: Q1 2026 adjusted operating earnings were $0.91 per share versus $0.92 a year earlier, ahead of expectations mainly on favorable weather and timing items (CEO Calvin Butler / CFO Jeanne Jones). 2026 guidance of $2.81-$2.91 per share affirmed, with the goal of the midpoint or better. Long-term 2025-2029 operating earnings growth outlook affirmed near the top end of the 5%-7% range. The CFO expects Q2 earnings at approximately 15% of the guidance midpoint, which would put 47% of full-year earnings in the first half.
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 adj EPS $0.91 vs $0.92; 2026 guide $2.81-$2.91 affirmed; growth near top end of 5%-7% through 2029

quarterly_data.signal: The CFO described a revised four-year capital plan that shifts money from distribution to transmission for data-center load: nearly $10 billion in 2026 and $41.7 billion over four years. The revision includes $1.1 billion of project deferrals and reductions in PECO and BGE distribution, offset by $1.5 billion of incremental transmission investment. That investment supports project realignment and the interconnection of data center customers that have signed Transmission Security Agreements. Annualized rate base growth is maintained at 7.9%. Separately, the CEO said PECO withdrew its recently filed electric and gas rate cases on customer-affordability grounds, calling it a timing decision that shows Exelon can adjust timing and reallocate capital. The CFO said the new transmission work was already on the horizon and aligned to some of the cluster studies.
quarterly_data.figure: $1.5 billion of incremental transmission investment; $1.1 billion of project deferrals and reductions; $41.7 billion over the next four years; 7.9% rate base growth

quarterly_data.signal: The CFO now expects transmission rate base to grow at 16% through 2029, citing growth driven by reliability requirements and large load interconnections. The $12 billion-$17 billion upside opportunity beyond the planning period is maintained. That range does not include the recent MISO competitive transmission bids or potential solar or storage opportunities.
quarterly_data.figure: transmission rate base growing at 16% through 2029; upside $12 billion-$17 billion unchanged

quarterly_data.signal: The CEO said Exelon is working to back its data center pipeline increasingly with FERC-approved Transmission Security Agreements. Those agreements have now secured approximately $1 billion of collateral.
quarterly_data.figure: Transmission Security Agreements have secured approximately $1 billion of collateral

quarterly_data.signal: Competitive transmission push: in February Exelon submitted bids for 2 Illinois transmission opportunities in the MISO Tranche 2.1 window, pursued jointly with Invenergy (not a graph node). The CEO said 2 additional bids are expected later this month and that Exelon will keep bidding in future transmission windows across PJM and other ISOs. He also said Exelon is looking at partnerships to build contracted generation, with nothing announced yet.
quarterly_data.figure: approximately $1.9 billion of total transmission capital spend (2 MISO Tranche 2.1 bids)

quarterly_data.signal: PJM supply shortage as seen by Exelon management. The CEO said customers paid $32 billion to generators for capacity in PJM over the last two years while supply declined by 1.2 gigawatts, and that Mid-Atlantic residential supply costs rose by up to 80% or more over five years. Exelon's Colette Honorable said PJM reported 811 new generation projects capable of 220 GW applying to interconnect. She noted only 19% of queued projects reach operation, and that 54 GW already cleared are delayed by siting, permitting, and supply chain issues.
quarterly_data.figure: $32 billion paid to generators for capacity in PJM; supply declined by 1.2 gigawatts; 54 GW cleared but delayed; only 19% of queued projects reach operation

quarterly_data.signal: Cost actions: $350 million of incremental O&M savings in 2027, tied to work Exelon will no longer pursue and described as largely sustainable. The CFO said the savings come partly from accelerating AI and technology transformation, fewer outside contractors, managed hiring and a targeted voluntary separation program later this year. Adjusted O&M growth is targeted at no more than 2% through 2029, and a 9%-10% consolidated ROE is expected for 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: $350 million of incremental O&M savings in 2027; no more than 2% adjusted O&M growth through 2029

quarterly_data.signal: Financing: approximately 43% ($2.3 billion) of planned 2026 long-term debt financing is complete, including all expected corporate and Pepco Holdings debt transactions for the year. The plan through 2029 is funded with about $21.8 billion of internally generated cash flow, $13.1 billion of utility debt, $3.4 billion of holding company debt and $3.4 billion of equity. All of the $850 million 2026 equity need and over $400 million for 2027 are priced via ATM forward contracts. The credit metric target is approximately 14% at Moody's and S&P. The CFO said PECO is on review for a downgrade.
quarterly_data.figure: approximately 43% or $2.3 billion of planned long-term debt financing completed; $3.4 billion of equity through 2029; $850 million in equity needs for 2026 priced
